source: Motion, Creative Benchmarks 2026
rule: On Meta the plain-text ad and the product picture with words on it win more often than the expensive production.
result: Hit rate: text only 11.60 % (1,728 winners), product image with text 8.75 % (6,256), UGC 7.56 % (11,374), high production 6.97 % (2,653), lifestyle image with text 6.10 % (8,769), carousel 4.45 % (15); spend ratio text only 1.97, product image with text 1.23, UGC 1.00, high production 0.79
measured_by: Motion, 578,750 Meta ads
holds: Meta feeds, holiday season, advertisers using Motion
fails: Not video-only: mixes stills and video
how_to_use: Always include one text-only and one product-with-words cut among the openings
doubt: text ads are cheap, so better offers may be put on them

source: Motion, Creative Benchmarks 2026
rule: As a first picture, unboxing, an offer banner, behind the scenes, the founder and POV win more often than a review, a list, a split screen or before-and-after.
result: Hit rate: unboxing 9.83 % (1,229 winners), offer-first banner 8.68 % (11,006), behind the scenes 8.64 % (772), founder 8.57 % (692), POV 8.28 % (792), demo 8.11 % (5,563), grid swap 7.98 % (882), influencer 7.71 % (635), montage 7.02 % (3,704), testimonial 6.57 % (5,073), before and after 6.07 % (1,724), listicle 5.30 % (1,641), review 4.89 % (804)
measured_by: Motion, 578,750 Meta ads
holds: Meta, holiday; differs by trade (education unboxing 22.54 %)
fails: Trade tables have thin cells with ratios like 1.00 that mean very few ads
how_to_use: Start a seller’s set with: hands opening the box, the owner at work, the offer on a banner, the product doing its job
doubt: observational; AI tags

source: WPP Media, System1, TikTok, The Creator Effectiveness Playbook, 2026
rule: Put the brand into the first two seconds of a creator video: those with strong two-second branding leave about three times the memory of those with weak.
result: creator ads +196 % Brand Memory Lift (343 vs 116 index), brand-made ads +47 % (147 vs 100), top vs bottom 20 % on two-second recognition
measured_by: TikTok Brand Lift Studies (exposed vs matched control) joined to System1 panel of TikTok users; 337 campaigns: 195 brand-made, 142 creator; 8 markets; advertisers’ money (about $70.5M over 1,217 ads), study by sellers TikTok, System1, WPP
holds: paid TikTok, US UK DE FR IT ES BR MX
fails: memory, not sales; authors say it is not causal
how_to_use: Write the brand into the hook itself: in the hand, in the place, in the first sentence
doubt: observational between ads

source: WPP Media, System1, TikTok, The Creator Effectiveness Playbook, 2026
rule: Say the brand and show it in the opening: doing both doubles how many people recognise it against showing only.
result: Two-second recognition: no cue 7.5 %, show only 25.7 %, say only 45.4 %, say and show 53.1 %; only 18 % of creator ads use early sound
measured_by: System1 Test Your Ad Social, 620 paid creator ads, 93,000 TikTok users, forced-choice panel in a skippable feed
fails: recognition, not buying; the print prose says 2x visual only, the bars 53.1 vs 25.7
how_to_use: Opening line names the product, opening picture shows it
doubt: chart order of say-only and show-only read from the extracted text positions

source: WPP Media, System1, TikTok, The Creator Effectiveness Playbook, 2026
rule: Use two to four brand signs in the first two seconds; with more than four attention drops and the memory falls.
result: Memory peak at four cues (scaled 78.3), raw lift range 3.1-7.5 %; attention index 100 at none, 62 around three to four
measured_by: System1, 620 creator ads, 93,000 users, partly modelled lift
fails: attention is lower at any brand cue than at none; modelled
how_to_use: Cap: name spoken, name written, pack in the hand, sound; no fifth
doubt: exact attention values per bar cannot be matched from the text

source: WPP Media, System1, TikTok, The Creator Effectiveness Playbook, 2026
rule: Early brand sound, logo inside the scene, spoken name and written name help memory; brand colours and a bare product shot in the opening hurt it when they interrupt.
result: highest lift sonic asset (about +3 points vs average, used by fewer than 5 %), then logo in context, spoken name, written name; brand colours, product, slogan, font below average
measured_by: System1 620 creator ads, 93,000 users, part measured part modelled
fails: differences are about 1-3 points and directional
how_to_use: Prefer a spoken name and a sign that is in the scene over a product close-up as the first frame. Corrects round one, which named the spoken brand name as top; the source puts sonic assets top
doubt: directional

source: WPP Media, System1, TikTok, The Creator Effectiveness Playbook, 2026
rule: Openings that put on a little show (a place people know, a face changing, something out of the ordinary, a story) hold people; openings that lecture (many words, facts and comparisons, split screen, talking straight at you) are skipped.
result: Most vs least entertaining creator ads: +82 % 6-second view-through (index 183 vs 100), stars 2.7 vs 2.2; something out of the ordinary has the biggest attention gain
measured_by: System1, 620 creator ads, 93,000 TikTok users (attention = 6-second VTR)
holds: TikTok paid creator ads, awareness aims
fails: System1’s 2025 report: ads heavy with salesmanship had more conversion lift (+88 %), so this is for memory and watching
how_to_use: For a brand job open with the unusual event; for a sale job use the demo and the price
doubt: the two goals conflict

source: WPP Media, System1, TikTok, The Creator Effectiveness Playbook, 2026
rule: Too many words on screen, a hard call to action, and a self-conscious presenter each lower what people feel about a creator ad.
result: stars: many words on screen -12 %, self-consciousness -8.8 %, "told me to do something" -7.3 %
measured_by: System1, 620 creator ads, 93,000 TikTok users
fails: not buying; TikTok retail data show call to action with price lifting conversion
how_to_use: Short words on screen and a natural presenter; keep the order to act for the sales cut
doubt: feature association

source: WPP Media, System1, TikTok, The Creator Effectiveness Playbook, 2026
rule: A high engagement rate tells you almost nothing about whether the brand was remembered.
result: engagement rate explains 0.2 % of Brand Memory Lift, comments-to-likes 11.3 %, emotion 28.1 %, emotion plus early branding 54.6 %
measured_by: 231 TikTok Brand Lift Studies including 90 creator campaigns, 129.6m engagements
fails: not tested on sales
how_to_use: Do not pick the winner hook by likes; use recall or sales test
doubt: sellers of the emotion metric are the authors

source: WPP Media, System1, TikTok, The Creator Effectiveness Playbook, 2026
rule: A recognised creator whose world fits the brand doubles memory; fit counts for more than fame.
result: index: low fit low fame 100, high fame only 110, high fit only 135, both 189; emotion +58 % with fit vs +23 % with fame, attention +17 % vs +10 %
measured_by: 239 UK-coded creator ads, 35,850 TikTok users, modelled lift
fails: modelled
how_to_use: Choose the creator whose everyday scene already contains the product and open in that scene
doubt: modelled, UK only

source: System1 + TikTok, The Long and the Short (form) of It, 2025, full report

result: -51 % conversion lift, top vs bottom quartile of 6-second view-through
measured_by: System1 Test Your Ad Social, 847 TikTok ads, 84,788 TikTok users, 8 markets, matched with 119 locally run TikTok Conversion Lift studies (exposed vs control; advertisers’ own money; run by TikTok, sellers)
fails: observational between campaigns; view-through is not the same as hook rate
how_to_use: Never choose a sales hook by view-through alone; choose by incremental sales or at least by conversions
doubt: 119 studies, effect partly because sales ads are made to make people leave the video

source: System1 + TikTok, The Long and the Short (form) of It, 2025, full report
rule: A small brand sells more on TikTok with an entertaining opening than with a hard sell; a famous brand can sell hard.
result: Conversion lift, small brands: entertaining 2.4x (90 to 215), hard-sell features +41 % (102 to 144). Category leaders: hard-sell 3.5x (44 to 155), entertaining +29 % (93 to 120)
measured_by: System1 Test Your Ad Social, 847 TikTok ads, 84,788 TikTok users, 8 markets, 119 Conversion Lift studies, split by brand size, top vs bottom quartile

how_to_use: For the dentist or the furniture maker open on a story, a funny or strange event or a face; keep the direct price pitch for a brand everybody knows or for the second video
doubt: contradicts the one-size advice of round one

source: System1 + TikTok, The Long and the Short (form) of It, 2025, full report
rule: For a small brand, showing the brand in the first two seconds helped memory but lowered conversion; for a famous brand it raised conversion.

measured_by: System1 Test Your Ad Social, 847 TikTok ads, 84,788 TikTok users, 8 markets, 119 Conversion Lift studies, top vs bottom quartile
fails: cells not sized in the report; not a test of one ad with and without brand
how_to_use: For a small seller do not waste second one on the logo: use feeling first, brand as part of the scene; brand-first only for known names
doubt: round one said early brand costs nothing; that is true for memory only

source: System1 + TikTok, The Long and the Short (form) of It, 2025, full report
rule: Entertaining openings also convert: most versus least entertaining TikTok ads had +50 % conversion lift and double the awareness lift.

measured_by: System1 Test Your Ad Social, 847 TikTok ads, 84,788 TikTok users, 8 markets, 358 locally run TikTok Brand and Conversion Lift studies, top vs bottom quartile

source: System1 + TikTok, The Long and the Short (form) of It, 2025, full report
rule: The first impression sets the ceiling: ads that raise brand choice on first view go on at about 4.5 times the rate of weak ones, and repeating cannot fix a weak opening.
result: +88 % brand choice from the first exposure; top vs bottom quartile 4.5x
measured_by: System1, controlled experiment, 8,000 TikTok users, 40 ads, 6 markets, 80,000+ exposures (brand choice before and after)

how_to_use: Test the opening on a first view; drop the weak one instead of raising frequency

measured_by: System1 Test Your Ad Social, 847 TikTok ads, 84,788 TikTok users, 8 markets, matched with 239 TikTok Brand Lift studies (with vs without)

measured_by: System1 Test Your Ad Social, 847 TikTok ads, 84,788 TikTok users, 8 markets, 119 Conversion Lift studies, top vs bottom quartile of neutrality

result: 2.7x relative brand lift (footnote says multiplied by 3)
